newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Singapore ship off Hong Kong repaired.
newsitem.headline: Singapore ship off Hong Kong repaired.

text.p: Half of the crew of a Singapore-owned ship were evacuated by helicopter south of Hong Kong on Sunday after its engines failed in heavy seas, but the vessel was later cleared to continue its voyage after repairs, a Hong Kong government spokesman said.

Eleven of the 24-man crew of the Equator Pearl, owned by the Singapore-based Thong Soon Lines Private Limited, were evacuated by a Hong Kong rescue team 110 miles south of the British colony. The rest of the crew, including the captain, remained to carry out repairs.
Timothy Li, a spokesman for the Marine Department which co-ordinated the rescue, said by telephone the captain had declared the ship safe to sail on after the repairs.

The owner of the Vessel, en route to Taiwan's Keelung from Singapore, could not be immediately reached for comment. Hong Kong had sent rescuers in two helicopters to the scene at 0530 GMT to carry out the airlift, a government statement said.
At 0230, the Hong Kong Marine Department had received a report from the captain saying that the ship had engine trouble.
The department sent search aircraft from the Government Flying Service to the scene and alerted ships in the area to help. The vessel was later located by the aircraft.
About an hour later, the captain decided to abandon the ship because of rough seas, the statement said.

Singapore Radio, which also picked up a may-day call at 0337 GMT, reported the 8,447 DWt (dead weight tonnes) vessel was in a dangerous situation with the ship listing 45 degrees in very rough seas as a typhoon approached.
The vessel was positioned at latitude 20.10.8 north and longitude 114.08.5 east when it sent out the signal, Singapore Radio said.
